title: Commissioning Vendor Acceptance & SLA Escalation Readout

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-03-05
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Avery Chen (Redwood AE); Jordan Patel (Redwood SE); Maya Singh (Arcadia - Procurement); Dylan Park (Arcadia - Legal); Sofia Rojas (Arcadia - Platform Security)

Auto Summary (auto): We reviewed MSA/DPA exceptions, discussed SLA metrics and escalation ladder for production ingestion, and scoped a 90-day pilot with dedicated capacity and KMS expectations. Pricing conversation focused on committed volume vs pay-as-you-go.

Transcript:
[00:00] Avery (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you making time. quick roll call, and then Jordan will jump into the technical constraints.
[00:12] Maya (Arcadia): Hi, Maya here. thanks. we're on procurement side and I wanna make sure the MSA path is clear.
[00:17] Dylan (Arcadia - Legal): Dylan here. I'll be focusing on DPA, audit logs, and esc- -- excuse me, escalation terms.
[00:24] Jordan (Redwood SE): Jordan here. I'll cover the SSO/KMS and latency SLOs. FYI, some of the slides I sent earlier had a typo, it says "RedWood Dedicated" — that's our dedicated offering.
[00:34] Avery: Great, okay Jordan you want to start with the SLA ask?
[00:38] Jordan: Sure. So Arcadia's initial ask was 99.95 uptime and p95 latency under 350 ms for the inference path at 2k rps, is that right Maya?
[00:50] Maya: That's the target, yes. We can be flexible on p99 as long as there's an escalation ladder and credits.
[00:58] Dylan: We also want automatic failover to a fallback model in a separate region, and explicit data handling for EU-resident PII.
[01:07] Jordan: Okay. The platform supports fallback routing, yes. The tricky part is the KV cache behavior across regions, sometimes the transcript of the cache -- I mean the KV cache can warm up and cause a tail-latency blip, so we recommend a warmup window during rollouts.
[01:25] Maya: That tail latency is a key procurement risk; can you define typical warmup?
[01:29] Jordan: Typically 30 to 90 seconds depending on prompt diversity, but for our Dedicated pool we can pre-warm for the pilot. We'll document the expected distribution.
[01:38] Sofia (Arcadia - Security): Quick question, on KMS: do you support customer-managed keys in our AWS KMS or HSM? and can logs be exported to our SIEM?
[01:47] Jordan: Yes, we support CMKs via our private deployment path; logs can be pushed to your splunk or cloudwatch, there's a small agent. There's also an audit log retention option.
[01:56] Dylan: On audit logs, we need immutable logs with S3 object lock or similar for a 7-year retention window. Is that possible?
[02:04] Avery: We have an add-on for extended retention that uses append-only storage; it's not out-of-the-box S3 object lock in all configs but we can map the contract to the right storage option. I'll follow up with the ops team.
[02:15] Maya: and SOC2? you said you were SOC2 accredited in the deck. we need a timeline for the next audit and evidence available to customers.
[02:23] Jordan: We're SOC2 Type II in our hosted service; for Dedicated/private there's a separate attestation. We can provide the cert and a scope doc, plus an optional on-site audit playbook for enterprise.
[02:35] Dylan: For the DPA, two clauses to note: subprocessing list inclusion and data residency carve-outs. Also, indemnity on data breaches — we want clearer liability caps tied to SLA breaches.
[02:47] Avery: Understood. Our standard MSA caps are X months of fees, but for enterprise we can negotiate. For SLA credits, we usually do percentage credits for monthly invoice, can be tiered.
[02:58] Maya: procurement will want the SLA credit schedule spelled out in the SOW, including the escalation contacts and time-to-response windows.
[03:07] Jordan: We'll provide an escalation ladder: Sev1 15 min ack, 60 min eng response; Sev2 1 hr ack, 4 hr eng response — those are examples. For production we can agree tighter windows.
[03:21] Dylan: We also need to ensure there's a rollback SLA for canary deployments — if a rollout increases p99 beyond baseline, there needs to be an automatic rollback trigger.
[03:31] Jordan: We have rollback policies in the console, yes. They can be set to auto-fallback to previous model or region. We'll send screenshots of the rollout config.
[03:40] Maya: Pricing, high level: your pricing deck had a commit discount tiers. procurement needs to know the minimum commitment and the exit terms if pilot doesn't convert.
[03:49] Avery: For the 90-day pilot we recommended a small reserved capacity plus burst, no long-term commitment required. Post-pilot there are tiered reserved options — monthly commit for Dedicated.
[03:58] Maya: For approvals, finance requires a not-to-exceed number for the pilot. can you give a capped estimate?
[04:04] Jordan: We can model it. If you give us expected peak qps and average token length, we can produce a capped pilot quote.
[04:12] Maya: we'll send traffic profile after the call.
[04:15] Dylan: Back to DPA redlines — our legal team wants a clause that prohibits sublicensing of customer data to third parties, and strong encryption in transit and at rest.
[04:25] Avery: That's standard, we can put that in. Regarding sublicensing, we do have subprocessors for infra (cloud provider) but we list them in the subprocessor registry; we can carve exceptions but we'll need to ensure it's acceptable.
[04:39] Sofia: Also curious about egress charges for data leaving region — procurement needs to budget for that.
[04:45] Jordan: Egress is a pass-through charge in some deployments; for Dedicated we can localize inference to avoid cross-region egress.
[04:52] Maya: okay. one more security note — SSO: we require SAML 2.0 with SCIM for provisioning. can you integrate with our Okta?
[04:59] Jordan: Yes, Okta + SCIM is supported, though we had one customer who had a tricky claim mapping issue — the attribute names can vary. we'll provide a config checklist.
[05:10] Dylan: Are there any data escrow or escrow-like protections for model weights? we have regulatory folks asking because models may be part of a critical path for payment decisions.
[05:20] Avery: We don't escrow model weights by default. For regulated customers we have an enterprise option to escrow artifacts; that's negotiable and would go into the contract.
[05:29] Maya: Sounds good. procurement timeline: we need redlines back within a week ideally so the commercial committee can review. is that realistic?
[05:36] Avery: Yes — we can turn a DPA redline matrix and updated pricing in 3 business days. Jordan will send the technical artifacts in parallel.
[05:45] Jordan: I'll attach an ops runbook: KMS diagram, SSO mapping example, rollback policy, and a note about KV cache warmup for canaries.
[05:55] Dylan: On SLA credits again — will you accept a tiered credit that increases if multiple SLA violations occur in a quarter?
[06:03] Avery: We can do a cumulative credit schedule; the exact thresholds are negotiable. We'll propose one and you can counter.
[06:10] Maya: one last thing — training data retention: do you retain prompts or PII? and do customers have an opt-out?
[06:18] Jordan: For the hosted API we have an opt-out for data usage for training, customers can request that. For Dedicated/private the data stays in your VPC unless you share telemetry. We'll document exact retention defaults.
[06:29] Sofia: Are you able to provide an extract of logs for e-discovery requests?
[06:33] Jordan: Yes, exportable audit logs are available; there's a small permissioning flow.
[06:38] Maya: ok let's wrap with explicit next steps. Avery?
[06:41] Avery: Yeah — recap: Redwood sends DPA redline matrix, updated pilot pricing (capped estimate), and SE runbook with KMS/SSO diagrams by next Monday 2025-03-10. Arcadia will return MSA redlines by 2025-03-12 and provide traffic profile to Jordan. Then schedule pilot kick-off the week of 2025-03-17.
[06:59] Dylan: sounds good. please include the escalation contacts and the specific time windows in the SOW.
[07:05] Avery: will do. Jordan anything else technical?
[07:08] Jordan: I'll also include some sample metrics from similar payments customers — tail latency curves and tokenization cost estimates.
[07:15] Maya: thanks, everyone. that helps procurement route this.
[07:18] Avery: Great, thanks all. We'll follow up by email.

End transcript.
